qs.q: What were the micro-average AUC, F1 and accuracy in the internal testing cohort, and how many slides did it contain?
What F1 did the system and the three pathologists reach in five-fold cross-validation?
qs.a: System 0.871; the three pathologists 0.851, 0.849 and 0.852 (average 0.851); Fleiss kappa among pathologists 0.823

qs.q: Under what condition did the pathologists diagnose the slides, and does the paper report a significance test for system versus pathologists?
qs.a: They already knew each slide was one of DLBCL, FL or HL. No statistical test of the 0.871 vs 0.851 difference is reported (box plots only)

qs.q: For which lymphoma type was the system worse than the pathologists, and what do the authors say is the reason?
qs.a: Hodgkin lymphoma (system F1 0.751, sensitivity 0.631); all nine backbone models were inferior to the pathologists for HL. The authors infer that multiple-instance aggregation attenuates the local attention on Hodgkin cells

qs.q: Why does the paper report two different micro-average F1 values for the system, 0.887 and 0.871?
qs.a: They come from different evaluations: 0.887 is the single internal testing split, 0.871 is the average over five-fold cross-validation. They are not the same measurement and should not be mixed

qs.q: Did the paper show that the Swin Transformer backbone is significantly better than the other eight backbones?
qs.a: No. It had the highest micro AUC 0.955 (0.942-0.969) and F1 0.887 vs 0.935 and 0.877 for InceptionV3, but formal pairwise significance testing was not performed (paired predictions were not retained); the authors state this as a limitation

qs.q: What did the external validation cover, and what accuracy did the system reach there?
qs.a: Only DLBCL slides from surgical resections: 203 from TCIA (accuracy/F1 0.783 +- 0.069) and 26 from TCGA (0.846 +- 0.091). The model was trained on biopsies from a single hospital

qs.q: Which limitations do the authors list?
qs.a: Only three common subtypes; weaker Hodgkin identification than pathologists; single-centre training and external sets with only DLBCL; no clinical or molecular data

qs.q: By how much did the system reduce the number of immunohistochemistry stains or the diagnostic turnaround time?
qs.a: NOT STATED. The abstract only says it could potentially reduce supplementary tests; no reduction was measured

qs.q: How long does the system take to process one slide?
qs.a: NOT STATED. No inference time or compute cost is reported
